docs.title: s1-rainfall-coherence
docs.text:
Code and data for A global dose–response for rainfall and Sentinel-1 interferometric coherence, Li et al.

Coherence loss was measured over 21,010 rainfall events, each set against a dry interferogram of the same burst, the same twelve-day baseline and the same season. The relationship is logarithmic and has no threshold.

\[L = 0.82 + 5.27\,\log_2 R\]

for \(L\) the percentage by which the coherence of the event pair falls below its control and \(R\) the 24 h accumulation in millimetres.

docs.title: What the study found
docs.text:
mean reduction against a dry control 11.8%, 95% interval 11.2 to 12.4 per doubling of the accumulation 5.27 percentage points at 1–3 mm, where practice assumes nothing happens 6.0% zero point, measured not assumed +0.17% on dry-against-dry pairs tree cover against grassland, same storm +3.4 points built-up against grassland −5.4 points

The headline is weighted to the census of 166,117 events the units were drawn from, since every event above 15 mm was processed while lighter events were sampled. Unweighted, the processed units give 19.2%, which describes the sample rather than the rainfall.

The effect begins far below the accumulations usually treated as extreme. Half of the maximum loss is reached by 10 mm, so routine light rainfall is a systematic contributor to temporal decorrelation and is not currently screened for in operational processing.

docs.title: Two ways to use this repository
docs.text:
Reproduce the analysisRebuild from the archive

The 27 MB of tables ship with the repository. No download, no raw imagery, no Earth Engine account, no cluster.

pip install -e .
rcoh fit

See Getting the data and Reproducing the paper.

Start from 00_unit_manifest.csv, pull the Sentinel-1 bursts from ASF, form the interferograms, and run the full pipeline.

This needs a cluster, an Earth Engine account and some weeks. See the Pipeline overview.

docs.title: Design in one paragraph
docs.text:
A unit is one rainfall event expressed as a comparison between two interferograms of the same burst stack. The case pair spans the event, one acquisition having received the rain and the other, twelve days away, less than 1 mm. The control pair is dry at both acquisitions and is drawn from the same burst, the same baseline and the same season, so that the ground and the interval are held in common and only the weather differs. Their ratio is the unit's measurement of the loss.

Why a ratio and not a difference

Coherence magnitude is specific to the processing chain. A ratio survives a change of scale between chains; an absolute difference in coherence does not. Neither survives a change of noise floor, so the reductions here are comparable with another study in their ordering and form, not in their magnitudes.

docs.title: Getting the data
docs.text:
There is nothing to get. The nine tables and the manifest the analysis reads, 27 MB in all and licensed CC-BY 4.0, ship with the repository in data/.

git clone https://github.com/jldz9/s1-rainfall-coherence
cd s1-rainfall-coherence
pip install -e .
rcoh population          # no download, no configuration

The loaders find data/ by walking up from the installed package, so this works from any working directory in an editable install.

Reading a copy held elsewhere

Set RCOH_DATA to override the bundled tables, or pass root= to any loader. The same tables are archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.XXXXXXX, which is the citable form; the copy here exists so that a reviewer need not fetch anything.

export RCOH_DATA=/path/to/deposit

docs.title: What is in the deposit
docs.text:
file rows what it holds 00_unit_manifest.csv 21,010 burst and the four acquisition dates of every unit 01_units_analysed.parquet 21,010 the analysed sample, one row per unit 02_units_by_landcover.parquet 221,229 coherence resolved by cover class within each unit 03_validation_arm.parquet 1,907 dry-against-dry pairs; the zero point and the floor 04_shared_control_arm.parquet 4,936 rainfall and dry pairs against one shared control 05_rain_masked.parquet 23,015 coherence and rainfall over wetted pixels only 06_perpendicular_baselines.parquet 89,069 perpendicular baseline per interferogram 07_within_burst_wet_dry.parquet 4,167 wetted against unwetted ground in one image 08_soil_water.parquet 25,768 ERA5-Land soil water at all four acquisitions 09_event_census.parquet 166,117 every rainfall event screened, for the population weights

Column-by-column definitions are in the data dictionary.

docs.title: What is not in the deposit
docs.text:
The interferograms

31,580 burst groups at roughly 75 MB each, some 300 GB. They are not deposited because they are regenerable, and because the Sentinel-1 bursts they derive from are Copernicus open data already archived at the Alaska Satellite Facility.

00_unit_manifest.csv is the bridge. It gives the burst identifier and the four acquisition dates of every unit, so the whole store can be rebuilt:

unit_id                   burst            t_event     t_ref       t_sec       ctrl_ref    ctrl_sec
t001_000033_iw1_20150602  t001_000033_iw1  2015-06-02  2015-05-21  2015-06-02  2017-05-10  2017-05-22

See the Pipeline overview for the rebuild.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
from rainfall_coherence import io

u = io.units()            # 21,010 rows, with reduction_pct and headroom
c = io.landcover()        # cover-resolved, restricted to analysed units
v = io.validation()       # dry-against-dry
s = io.soil_water()       # with dtheta oriented to the event
m = io.masked()           # loss_all and loss_wet side by side
w = io.within_burst()     # with the within-unit difference
b = io.baselines()        # perpendicular baselines

Each loader attaches the derived columns the analysis needs, so a caller never recomputes a reduction by hand or merges the soil-water table unoriented.

Do not re-filter

io.landcover() deliberately does not apply the headroom condition, and io.soil_water() orients the change to the event. Both are described in Pitfalls; getting either wrong changes published results.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The package splits into two halves. The analysis half reads the deposited tables and needs nothing but the scientific Python stack. The extraction half reads coherence rasters and talks to Earth Engine, and is only needed if you intend to rebuild from the archive.

Analysis onlyWith extraction

Everything needed to reproduce the tables, the figures and Equation 3 from the data deposit.

A fresh environment 
conda create -n rcoh python=3.12
conda activate rcoh

git clone https://github.com/jldz9/s1-rainfall-coherence
cd s1-rainfall-coherence
pip install -e .

Pulls numpy, pandas, pyarrow, scipy and matplotlib.

Adds raster reading and Earth Engine, for phases 01 to 03 of the pipeline.

pip install -e ".[extract]"
rasterio and GDAL

rasterio ships manylinux wheels with GDAL bundled, so pip alone usually suffices. If it fails to build, install GDAL from conda first:

conda install -c conda-forge gdal
pip install -e ".[extract]"

docs.title: Verifying the install
docs.text:
rcoh --help

With the data in place (see Getting the data):

# nothing to set: data/ ships with the clone
rcoh fit

  intercept            0.82
  slope                5.27
  r2_log               0.1032
  r2_linear            0.0764
  r2_sqrt              0.0991
  zero_mm              0.898
  n                    21010
  slope_above_15mm     6.46
  n_above_15mm         12272

If those match, the install reproduces Equation 3 of the paper.

docs.title: Checking every published number
docs.text:
pip install pytest
pytest

Eleven tests and twenty-nine assertions, each tied to a published number: the sample size, the headline reduction, Equation 3 and its comparison of functional forms, five rows of Table 4, the measurement floor, the within-burst difference, the masking sensitivity, and that the soil water change is oriented to the event. A pass means this install reproduces the published analysis exactly.

The suite runs against the bundled data/; set RCOH_DATA only to test a copy held elsewhere.

docs.title: Earth Engine
docs.text:
Only needed for 01_acquire/ and parts of 03_extract/. Authenticate once:

earthengine authenticate
Which scripts need it

build_events.py, build_covariates.py, extract_rainmasked.py, extract_rainfull.py and pull_cells.py. Each takes a --project argument naming your Earth Engine cloud project.

docs.text: Python ≥ 3.11 analysis numpy, pandas, pyarrow, scipy, matplotlib extraction rasterio, requests, earthengine-api disk, analysis only 25 MB for the deposit disk, full rebuild roughly 300 GB for the burst store

docs.title: Data dictionary
docs.text: Nine files, 25 MB, deposited at doi:10.5281/zenodo.XXXXXXX under CC-BY 4.0.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
A unit is one rainfall event expressed as a comparison between two interferograms of the same burst stack.

term meaning case the twelve-day pair spanning the event control a dry pair, same burst, same baseline, same season reduction (1 - g_case / g_ctrl) * 100, in percentage points headroom g_ctrl - 0.077; a unit needs 0.15 to be analysed

docs.title: 00_unit_manifest.csv — 21,010 rows
docs.text:
The file that makes the study rebuildable from the public archive.

column meaning unit_id burst and event date burst OPERA burst identifier t_event the day the rain fell t_ref, t_sec the two acquisitions of the case pair ctrl_ref, ctrl_sec the two acquisitions of the control pair lon, lat burst centre

docs.title: 01_units_analysed.parquet — 21,010 rows
docs.text: column meaning g_case, g_ctrl burst-mean coherence of the event and control pairs reduction_pct the headline quantity dgamma g_case - g_ctrl, in coherence units rain_mm IMERG 24 h accumulation, burst mean r0, r1 accumulation at the first and second case acquisition headroom g_ctrl - 0.077 koppen, season, dom_cover climate, hemisphere-corrected season, cover frac_gt1, frac_gt5, frac_gt15 fraction of the burst above 1, 5, 15 mm liquid_pct liquid fraction; below 90% is excluded btemp_days, n_px, doy baseline, valid pixels, day of year

docs.title: 02_units_by_landcover.parquet — 221,229 rows
docs.text:
One row per unit and cover class. cover is the WorldCover class, n_px its pixel count, g_case/g_ctrl its coherences.

Do not filter on headroom

See Pitfalls. It reverses the wetland sign.

docs.title: 03_validation_arm.parquet — 1,907 rows
docs.text: g_a, g_b are two dry interferograms of one burst; red is the signed contrast with the numerator assigned at random; ctrl is the nominated denominator; ddoy and dyear their separation in day of year and in years.

docs.title: 04_shared_control_arm.parquet — 4,936 rows
docs.text: g_shared serves as the denominator for both the rainfall pair (red_rain) and a second dry pair (red_dry); paired_diff is their within-unit difference.

docs.title: 05_rain_masked.parquet — 23,015 rows
docs.text: _all columns average over every valid land pixel, _wet over those in cells receiving 1 mm or more. rain_wet is the accumulation over the same wetted pixels, so response and dose share one support.

docs.title: 06_perpendicular_baselines.parquet — 89,069 rows
docs.text: One row per interferogram, role distinguishing case from control.

docs.title: 07_within_burst_wet_dry.parquet — 4,167 rows
docs.text: Wetted and unwetted populations of one interferogram, each with its own control baseline. d10–d90 are percentiles of the per-pixel difference.

docs.title: 08_soil_water.parquet — 25,768 rows
docs.text:
ERA5-Land volumetric_soil_water_layer_1 (0–7 cm), daily mean on each acquisition date.

Orient the change to the event

Δθ is θ(wet) − θ(dry). The wet acquisition is the one equal to t_event. Taking sec - ref cancels the sign for half the sample.

docs.title: 09_event_census.parquet — 166,117 rows
docs.text: Every rainfall event the units were drawn from, with its burst, date and IMERG accumulation. Needed for the population weights, since the sampling was stratified upon the accumulation.

docs.title: Products
docs.text: product use Sentinel-1 SLC, OPERA burst grid interferograms GPM IMERG V07 half-hourly rainfall; every accumulation reported CHIRPS daily, ERA5-Land daily candidate screening only, never a magnitude ERA5-Land hourly soil water, snow, temperature ESA WorldCover 2021 land cover Köppen-Geiger 1980–2016 climate class MODIS MOD13A2 NDVI

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
Two routes to the same numbers. Pick by whether you want to check the analysis or rebuild the measurement.

With the provided dataFrom scratch

A minute, on a laptop. Download the 25 MB deposit and every table, every fitted relationship and every figure in the paper regenerates.

pip install -e .
rcoh fit                 # Equation 3
rcoh dose                # Table 3
rcoh landcover           # Table 4
rcoh climate             # Table 5
rcoh floor               # the measurement floor

And the figures:

python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_dose          
python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_paired_arms   
python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_one_sidedness 
python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_baseline      
python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_r12_dose      
python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_rain_vs_moisture

This route starts from the measured coherences. It verifies the statistics, the fits and the figures, and it cannot verify the interferometry.

:material-arrow-right: Full walkthrough

Weeks, on a cluster. Retrieve the Sentinel-1 bursts, form the interferograms, measure the coherence, and rebuild the tables the other route starts from.

01_acquire    the burst grid, the S1 timeline, the rainfall census
     |
02_process    unit selection, then ~57,000 interferograms on SLURM
     |
03_extract    coherence over the rasters, soil water, baselines
     |
04_tables     the tables that are deposited
     |
(then the route on the left)

Needs an Earth Engine account, a SLURM cluster, roughly 300 GB, and InSARHub for the interferometry.

:material-arrow-right: Full walkthrough

docs.title: Which route verifies what
docs.text:
with the deposit from scratch the fitted relationships ✅ ✅ the tables and figures ✅ ✅ the cluster bootstrap and the intervals ✅ ✅ that the coherences were measured correctly ❌ ✅ that the units were selected correctly ❌ ✅ that the rainfall was retrieved correctly ❌ ✅ time a minute weeks hardware a laptop a cluster

A middle route

00_unit_manifest.csv in the deposit names the burst and the four acquisition dates of every unit, so you can rebuild the interferograms without repeating the event census or the unit selection. Start at 02 Process.

docs.title: Before either route
docs.text: Read Pitfalls. Three mistakes in handling these tables each changed a published number during the analysis, and two of them are silent — the result looks plausible and is wrong.

docs.title: 01 — Acquire
docs.text:
Establishing what exists before anything is processed: the burst grid, the Sentinel-1 acquisition timeline, the rainfall census, and the join between them.

script what it does build_burst_grid.py the static OPERA burst grid, 1,127,661 bursts, ~392,000 on land build_timeline.py the Sentinel-1 IW SLC acquisition timeline per burst build_events.py the rainfall census mark_affected.py joins the timeline to the census: which acquisitions carry rain verify_availability.py confirms every planned acquisition is actually retrievable profile_bursts.py land cover and Köppen class per burst

docs.title: The two-stage rainfall census
docs.text:
Screening is not measurement

build_events.py runs two stages, and conflating them is the commonest serious error in event-based remote sensing.

Stage A screens candidates from daily CHIRPS within 50° of the equator and ERA5-Land beyond it, taking the larger of the two. Both badly under-detect convective extremes:

product Derna, 10 September 2023 CHIRPS daily 3.3 mm ERA5 total precipitation 68.8 mm IMERG daily accumulation 206.7 mm

An order of magnitude, in exactly the gauge-sparse regions the campaign cares about. Stage A therefore sets its bar far below any threshold used in the analysis and serves only to find candidates.

Stage B measures with GPM IMERG V07 half-hourly on its native 0.1° grid, accumulated over the 24 h preceding each acquisition and averaged over the burst footprint. Every accumulation reported in the paper is a Stage B value.

docs.title: Event definition
docs.text:
An event is a single day within a two-degree cell, so a storm crossing several bursts is counted once. An event acquisition must reach 1 mm, the ETCCDI wet-day threshold.

Between 3 October 2014 and 23 September 2026 this gives 166,117 events across 2,764 burst stacks, of which 19,918 carry 15 mm or more.

One threshold, three jobs

1 mm is the floor an event must reach, the criterion deciding whether an acquisition is dry enough to enter a control pair, and the spatial mask separating wetted from dry ground within a burst. It is defined once, in config.WET_MM.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
from rainfall_coherence import io, tables, stats

tables.dose()                   # Table 3
tables.landcover_contrasts()    # Table 4
tables.climate_and_season()     # Table 5
tables.dose_relationship()      # Equation 3
tables.measurement_floor()      # the floor, by cover and climate

The headline, weighted to the event census:

tables.population_estimate()
# {'weighted_mean_pct': 11.76, 'ci': (11.17, 12.38),
#  'unweighted_mean_pct': 19.21, 'effective_n': 10873, ...}

The sample over-represents heavy rain roughly fivefold by design, so anything averaged across accumulations is weighted first. The unweighted mean of the processed units is available for comparison:

u = io.units()
stats.cluster_bootstrap(u.reduction_pct, u.burst, stat=lambda v: v.mean())
# (19.21, 18.63, 19.82) -- the sample, not the rainfall

The validation arm, which fixes the zero point:

v = io.validation()
stats.cluster_bootstrap(v.red, v.burst)     # (0.17, -0.69, 1.07)

The within-burst contrast, the one measurement immune to every confound because both populations lie in the same image under the same sky:

w = io.within_burst()
stats.cluster_bootstrap(w["diff"], w.burst) # (1.64, 1.33, 1.95)

docs.title: The figures
docs.text:
Each lands under the number it carries in the paper, as figN_*.png and figN_*.pdf.

figure command what it shows 3 python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_paired_arms the shared-control and within-burst contrasts 4 python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_one_sidedness the floor falls either way, the rainfall loss does not 5 python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_baseline the perpendicular baseline affects but cannot bias 6 python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_dose the dose–response 7 python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_r12_dose event and control coherence separately 8 python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.fig_rain_vs_moisture rainfall against soil water

All of them at once:

for f in fig_paired_arms fig_one_sidedness fig_baseline fig_dose \
         fig_r12_dose fig_rain_vs_moisture; do
    python -m rainfall_coherence.figures.$f
done
Options

fig_dose takes --linear to draw the same data on a linear axis, which is how the concavity was checked. fig_baseline and fig_paired_arms take further arguments documented in their module docstrings.

Figures 1 and 2

Figure 1 is a schematic, drawn by hand. The generator for Figure 2 is among the scripts being reconstructed; see the repository README.

docs.title: Verifying everything at once
docs.text:
pytest

Eleven tests and twenty-nine assertions, each tied to a published number: the sample size, the headline, Equation 3 and its form comparison, five rows of Table 4, the floor, the within-burst difference, the masking sensitivity, and that the soil-water change is oriented. A pass means this copy of the code reproduces the published analysis exactly. The suite runs against the bundled data/; RCOH_DATA need not be set.

One test is a tripwire

test_table3_landcover asserts that the wetland contrast is negative. It is negative in the published table and becomes positive if anyone reinstates the headroom filter on the land-cover rows. See Pitfalls.

docs.title: 03 — Extract
docs.text:
Measurement over the coherence rasters, and retrieval of everything else.

script produces extract_dgamma.py coherence resolved by land cover class extract_rainmasked.py coherence over rain-wetted pixels extract_rainfull.py coherence and accumulation over one identical pixel set extract_wetdry_within.py wetted against unwetted ground inside one interferogram build_covariates.py ERA5-Land soil water, NDVI, soil texture pull_cells.py soil water at all four acquisitions fetch_bperp.py perpendicular baselines from the ASF service

All take --root <store> and shard with --shard N --of M for a SLURM array.

docs.title: The within-burst contrast
docs.text:
extract_wetdry_within.py is the arm no confound touches. One rain mask, derived from the event day, is applied to both interferograms:

m = rain_mask_for(group, c_case, t_event)      # one mask, from the event
ok = land & finite(gc) & finite(gk) & (gc > 0) & (gk > 0)
wet, dry = ok & m, ok & ~m
stats(gc, gk, wet, "wet")     # both rasters, same selection
stats(gc, gk, dry, "dry")     # both rasters, same selection

Each population gets its own control baseline from the same control interferogram, which is what removes the "that patch is just rougher" explanation. The two populations also lie beneath one sky at one instant, so any tropospheric delay is common to them and cancels.

Why only 4,167 units qualify

A burst contributes only while a storm covers part of it. Units wholly wet or wholly dry are discarded, and each population must span at least one whole IMERG cell so that the comparison is of ground rather than of the burst outline clipping a cell corner.

docs.title: Masking both sides
docs.text:
extract_rainfull.py exists because masking the coherence while leaving the accumulation as a burst mean measures the response over one patch of ground and the dose over another. It retrieves the IMERG field itself rather than a threshold of it, caches it as float16 beside each burst, and averages coherence and accumulation over one identical pixel set.

Nearest neighbour, deliberately

The rain field is resampled to the coherence grid by nearest neighbour. An IMERG cell is a 0.1° block; interpolating it would invent a gradient across the wet edge that does not exist.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text: Three mistakes made during the analysis, each of which changed a published number before it was caught. The package guards against all three, but anyone working with the tables directly can still walk into them.

docs.title: 1. The headroom condition belongs to the unit
docs.text:
Never filter the land-cover table on headroom

# WRONG
d = io.landcover()
d = d[d.g_ctrl - 0.077 >= 0.15]     # do not do this

A control must stand 0.15 above the noise floor for a loss to be resolvable. That condition is a property of the unit, applied once to the burst mean when the analysed sample was built.

Applying it again to the rows of 02_units_by_landcover asks a different question — whether each cover class is bright — and conditions on the denominator of the very ratio being measured. It removes the dim covers preferentially:

cover median \(\gamma_{ctrl}\) correct with the stray filter rows dropped built-up 0.619 −5.4 −5.5 1% tree 0.388 +3.4 +4.0 11% wetland 0.357 −1.6 +1.6 21% snow and ice 0.371 −12.6 −6.2 30% mangrove 0.276 −4.1 +0.1 37%

The wetland contrast reverses sign. Snow and ice halves. The two covers quoted in the abstract barely move, which is why the error survived three attempts to find it.

io.landcover() does not apply the filter, and tables.landcover_contrasts() relies on that.

docs.title: 2. The soil water change must be oriented to the event
docs.text:
Δθ is wet minus dry, not second minus first

# WRONG
dtheta = theta_sec - theta_ref

The campaign allows the rain at either acquisition of a pair. Taking sec - ref inverts the sign for roughly half the sample, the two halves cancel, and the correlation with coherence loss collapses:

ρ with the reduction oriented, θ(wet) − θ(dry) +0.288 unoriented, θ(sec) − θ(ref) −0.086

The wet acquisition is the one equal to t_event. io.soil_water() orients it and exposes dtheta.

docs.title: 3. Resample bursts, never units
docs.text:
Units within a burst are not independent

# WRONG
bootstrap over rows

The 21,010 units occupy only 2,329 bursts, an average of nine to each and as many as forty-six, and units of one burst share its terrain and its scattering behaviour. Resampling units rather than bursts understates the spread by a factor of 1.7.

stats.cluster_bootstrap(u.reduction_pct, u.burst)   # groups = burst

Every interval in the paper is computed this way.

Pairing does not remove the clustering

Table 4 pairs each cover against grassland inside the same burst, which removes the burst from the contrast but not from the sampling: its units still share one terrain. Taken as \(sd/\sqrt{n}\) over units its standard errors ran 1.2 to 1.8 times too narrow, worst for tree cover. They resample bursts like every other interval in the paper.

docs.title: 4. Weight before averaging across accumulations
docs.text:
The sample over-represents heavy rain by design

# WRONG, if you want a population figure
io.units().reduction_pct.mean()      # 19.21%

Every event above 15 mm was processed where its acquisitions allowed, while lighter events were sampled for precision. So heavy rain is 58.4% of the units against 12.0% of the events recorded, and the unweighted mean describes the sample rather than the rainfall.

tables.population_estimate()["weighted_mean_pct"]    # 11.76%
unweighted weighted mean loss 19.21% 11.76% displacement noise 1.43 mm 0.88 mm falling below control 80.7% 72.4% median accumulation 16.5 mm 3.9 mm

Do not weight a conditional quantity

Table 3's bands, Eq. (3), the cover and climate contrasts and both validation arms are already conditioned on dose or paired within units. Weighting them adds noise without removing bias, and would change Eq. (3) from 0.82 + 5.27 log₂R to 1.46 + 4.98 log₂R for no gain.

The weighted headline is also the one that reconciles with the curve: the weighted median accumulation is 3.9 mm, for which Eq. (3) gives 11.2%.

docs.title: Two more worth knowing
docs.text:
A median is not additive. The median of the within-unit differences is not the difference of the two medians, and only the former respects the pairing. In the within-burst arm the wetted population falls 9.25% and the unwetted 6.05%, a gap of 3.20 — but the median paired difference is 1.64. Use stats.paired_difference.

Coherence magnitude is not portable. These values come from a phase-only estimator with an 11 × 11 Gaussian window on a 40 m pixel, 440 m square on the ground, and a floor of 0.077. A chain with a different window, a different multilook, a maximum-likelihood estimator or a Goldstein filter will not reproduce them, and will report different reductions. Compare the ordering and the form of the response, not the magnitudes.

One parameter is unresolved

The manuscript states the estimator's effective number of looks as 169 in one place and 133 in another. Both reach the 0.077 floor, by different conventions: \(1/\sqrt{169}=0.0769\) is the rms of the estimate at zero coherence, \(\sqrt{\pi}/(2\sqrt{133})=0.0768\) its mean. Neither matches the 102 an 11 × 11 Gaussian with \(\sigma=w/3\) would give on independent pixels, which is probably because the SHP test varies the sample per pixel. The floor itself is empirical and unaffected.

docs.title: 02 — Process
docs.text:
Choosing the units and forming the interferograms.

script what it does build_campaign.py unit selection: case and control pairing, the dry rules stage_groups.py materialises each processing group for the cluster submit_managed.py one SLURM job per group wx_submit_daemon.py sliding-window submitter, respecting the queue limits

docs.title: How a unit is built
docs.text:
For each qualifying event, build_campaign.py forms the case pair, a twelve-day interferogram straddling the rain, then searches the same burst stack for a control: a twelve-day pair, dry at both acquisitions, falling in the same season, and between one and five years from the event. Where several qualify, the one closest to the event's point in the year is taken.

WET_MM, DRY_MM = 15.0, 1.0   # see the warning below

WET_MM in this script is not the wet-day threshold

The name is misleading and is kept only because it is what was run. In build_campaign.py, written for the heavy arm:

constant value what it actually is WET_MM 15.0 the accumulation above which every available event was processed; below it events were sampled DRY_MM 1.0 the criterion deciding whether an acquisition is dry enough for a control

The paper's wet-day threshold is 1 mm, the ETCCDI definition, and that is also the event floor. 15 mm is a statement about coverage, not about rainfall. The package names them unambiguously as config.WET_DAY_MM, config.DRY_ACQ_MM and config.FULL_PROCESSING_MM.

Four conditions then reduce 30,593 formed units to the 21,010 analysed:

condition removes headroom: the control too near the noise floor 4,825 no liquid fraction returned by IMERG 112 snow or mixed phase, below nine tenths liquid 2,641 a non-event acquisition wetter than 1 mm 2,005

docs.title: The processing chain
docs.text:
Fixed for the whole study

parameter value backend ISCE3 / dolphin, driven through InSARHub DEM Copernicus GLO-30, buffered by 0.5° geocoding OPERA burst grid, 10 m range × 20 m azimuth multilook 4 range × 2 azimuth, giving a 40 m square pixel ionosphere JPL total electron content SHP selection generalised likelihood ratio test, significance 0.001 estimator phase-only window 11 × 11 Gaussian, σ = one third the window width window on the ground 11 × 40 m = 440 m square adaptive phase filter none noise floor 0.077 temporal baseline twelve days, every pair processed alone polarisation VV

The absence of a Goldstein filter is deliberate. It raises coherence most where coherence is lowest, which is where the rainfall cases sit, so filtering would compress the contrast under measurement by an amount that differs between chains.

docs.title: Cluster notes
docs.text:
Queue limits

The submitters assume a per-user cap on queued array tasks. Raise the throttle on a running array rather than cancelling and resubmitting:

scontrol update jobid=<id> MinCPUsNode=1 MinMemoryNode=4096
Checkpointing

The extraction scripts write their parquet every 100 units so a walltime kill cannot discard hours of Earth Engine retrieval. Resume with --skip-done.

docs.title: From scratch
docs.text:
Rebuilding the measurement itself: retrieve the imagery, form the interferograms, measure the coherence, assemble the tables, then run the analysis.

What this costs

The published study processed 56,930 interferograms across 31,580 burst groups. End to end this is weeks of cluster time and roughly 300 GB. If you want to check the statistics rather than the interferometry, use the deposit instead.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Earth Engine an authenticated cloud project cluster SLURM, or adapt the submitters disk ~300 GB for the burst store InSARHub forms the interferograms; installed separately this package pip install -e ".[extract]" 
earthengine authenticate
pip install -e ".[extract]"
export WX_ROOT=/path/to/the/store      # where everything is written

docs.title: The four phases
docs.text:
01_acquire    what exists, where it rained, which bursts were affected
     |
02_process    choose the units, stage them, form the interferograms
     |
03_extract    measure coherence over the rasters, pull the covariates
     |
04_tables     assemble the tables the analysis reads
     |
          then: With the provided data

docs.title: 01 — Acquire
docs.text:
Establish the burst grid, the acquisition timeline and the rainfall census, then join them.

python scripts/01_acquire/build_burst_grid.py     --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/01_acquire/build_timeline.py       --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/01_acquire/build_events.py         --root $WX_ROOT --project <ee-project>
python scripts/01_acquire/mark_affected.py        --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/01_acquire/verify_availability.py  --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/01_acquire/profile_bursts.py       --root $WX_ROOT --project <ee-project>

Produces the event census: 166,117 events over 2,764 burst stacks, of which 19,918 reach 15 mm. Details

Screening is not measurement

build_events.py screens candidates with CHIRPS and ERA5-Land, then measures every accumulation with IMERG. The screening products under-detect convective extremes by an order of magnitude. Never quote a Stage A value as a rainfall amount.

docs.title: 02 — Process
docs.text:
Select the units, stage them, and form the interferograms.

python scripts/02_process/build_campaign.py   --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/02_process/stage_groups.py     --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/02_process/wx_submit_daemon.py --root $WX_ROOT

The daemon submits a SLURM job per group and keeps a sliding window inside the queue limits. This is the phase that takes weeks. Details

Skipping phase 01

00_unit_manifest.csv in the deposit already names the burst and the four acquisition dates of every unit. Feed it to stage_groups.py and you skip the census and the selection entirely, reproducing the interferometry against exactly the published sample.

docs.title: 03 — Extract
docs.text:
Measure over the resulting rasters and retrieve everything else. All of these shard with --shard N --of M for a SLURM array.

python scripts/03_extract/extract_dgamma.py        --root $WX_ROOT --shard 0 --of 20
python scripts/03_extract/extract_wetdry_within.py --root $WX_ROOT --shard 0 --of 20
python scripts/03_extract/extract_rainfull.py      --root $WX_ROOT --shard 0 --of 20
python scripts/03_extract/build_covariates.py      --root $WX_ROOT --shard 0 --of 20
python scripts/03_extract/pull_cells.py            --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/03_extract/fetch_bperp.py           --root $WX_ROOT

Details

Checkpointing

Each writes its parquet every 100 units, so a walltime kill cannot discard hours of Earth Engine retrieval. Resume with --skip-done.

docs.title: 04 — Tables
docs.text:
Assemble the tables that the analysis reads.

python scripts/04_tables/build_paired_arms.py    --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/04_tables/build_validation_arm.py --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/04_tables/merge_and_analyse.py    --root $WX_ROOT
python scripts/04_tables/soil_moisture_arms.py   --root $WX_ROOT

Details

docs.title: Then the analysis
docs.text:
The outputs of phase 04 are the deposit. Point the package at them and continue exactly as in With the provided data:

export RCOH_DATA=$WX_ROOT/plan
rcoh fit

docs.title: Checking you landed in the same place
docs.text:
pytest

Eleven tests tied to published numbers. If your rebuild reproduces them, the chain matched; if test_equation_3 passes but the headline differs, the difference is in unit selection rather than in the interferometry.

Coherence magnitude is not portable

A different window, multilook or estimator will not reproduce the absolute coherences, and a chain applying a Goldstein filter will report smaller reductions. The parameters are fixed in 02 Process and every one of them matters. Compare the ordering and the form of the response before comparing magnitudes.

docs.title: 04 — Tables
docs.text:
Assembly of the deposited tables from the extraction outputs.

script writes build_paired_arms.py units_final, validation_arm, paired_rain_vs_null build_validation_arm.py the dry-against-dry pairs merge_and_analyse.py dgamma_all, the cover-resolved table soil_moisture_arms.py the soil-water join build_release_all.py the release tables landcover_rain.py the within-burst cover contrasts cell_counts.py per-cell diagnostics

docs.title: The three validation arms
docs.text:
The paper carries three independent constructions, all built here, and they count different objects. This is the commonest source of confusion:

arm n counts validation arm 1,907 pairs, one per burst shared control 4,936 rainfall units, 1,832 bursts unrestricted substitution 64,074 pairings, 1,751 bursts

The validation arm takes one pair per burst because pairs from a burst share ground and often an interferogram; seven controls would yield twenty-one pairs resting on seven measurements, and counting them all would narrow the bootstrap interval beyond what the evidence supports.

The shared-control arm is larger because several rainfall units can lean on the same control — a median of two, and as many as fourteen.

docs.title: Once these have run
docs.text:
Everything downstream is in the package rather than in scripts:

from rainfall_coherence import tables
tables.dose()
tables.landcover_contrasts()
tables.dose_relationship()

See Reproducing the paper.
